**RESUME HERE (cc, 2026-09-17 night, replacing doing 15 -- which asserted a peer's WITHDRAWN reading and knew nothing of the bump).** The read hv decision 25 asked for is DONE, JUDGED and BANKED. **Blocked on exactly one thing: hv's word that the full test suite is finished.** Do not infer that from `ps` -- four instruments lied to me tonight. Read `refs/bank/cc/bump/read` (blob 453f70fde) before touching any of this; it carries its own retraction at the end and the retraction is the important part.

**THE BUMP IS JUDGED, NOT LANDED. `rusqlite 0.40.2` / `libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2` / SQLite 3.53.2.** vc judged patch-id **8dbd56bbba9d232b81f5273a755f75bd47dc3df6** at `refs/bank/cc/bump/patch`; that id is what lands. Two files: `native/rust/Cargo.toml:85` `"0.32"` to `"0.40"`, and `crates/intentsvcs/src/store.rs:3199-3200` correcting the `BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` comment's citation from `rusqlite 0.32.1 / inner_connection.rs:119` to `0.40.2 / :118` -- verified, the default is still `sqlite3_busy_timeout(db, 5000)` across all eight minors and moved one line. **`git apply --check` passed; no cargo command has run.** `Cargo.lock` is NOT in the patch and must not be re-banked into it: vc judges the source, then inspects the lock at landing, and the acceptance condition is that **nothing moves except the rusqlite / libsqlite3-sys chain and its own transitive set. Anything else moving is a finding and STOPS the landing.**

**WHY IT IS A rusqlite BUMP AND NOT A libsqlite3-sys ONE:** the pin is lockstep caret at every release, so the sys crate cannot move a minor alone. Eight rusqlite minors, and **every named breaking change is inert for our code** -- 147 single-statement call sites with 0 multi-statement offenders, 0 typed `u64`/`usize` gets against 21 deliberate `as i64` casts, `cache` already a default feature for our one `prepare_cached`, 0 vtab impls, rustc 1.98.1 against an MSRV of 1.88.0. The one live site is `facade.rs:5039`, where the authorizer and progress handler register on a LOCAL OWNED connection, so 0.38.0's ownership check needs at worst a `mut`. **A static read settles the breaking changes a release NAMES and not the ones it does not; only the compile answers that.**

**THE REASON THE BUMP IS JUSTIFIED IS NOT THE ONE IN THE RULING, AND THIS MATTERS IF ANYONE RE-ARGUES IT.** hv decision 25 says the detector cannot be built on 3.46.0 "whose secure-delete allowance is one hard-coded leaf shape". **That special case is byte-identical at 3.46.0, 3.48.0 and 3.53.2 and the whole 149-line checker diffs to ZERO between 3.46.0 and 3.48.0.** No available version generalises it. 3.46.0's real defect is that the FTS5 4-to-5 version bump sits in `fts5UpdateMethod` (the vtab layer) and can lag the on-disk shape, so the checker's allowance never engages and it false-positives; 3.48.0 moves the write into `fts5FlushSecureDelete`. **That is a CODE READING, a hypothesis, and it must not enter 0442's body, RESULT-2.md or any bank as a mechanism (vc's instruction).** And the decisive reason is separate: **3.46.0 AND 3.48.0 both carry the WAL-reset database corruption bug** (sqlite.org/wal.html s11, present 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, fixed 3.51.3), whose preconditions -- WAL mode, two or more connections on one file in separate processes writing or checkpointing at the same instant -- are this estate by construction. **The bump is justified without the detector at all; the detector is the smaller half.**

**THE DETECTOR, AS RULED AFTER I RETRACTED MY OWN RECOMMENDATION. BUILD A2. DO NOT BUILD A1 AS THE 0442 DETECTOR.** A1 (`%_docsize` anti-joined against `%_content`) is **MEASURED BLIND** on the real damaged store: 0 both directions against non-empty populations of 829 and 829. `sqlite3Fts5StorageDelete` deletes index records, then `%_docsize`, then `%_content`, each gated on the previous, so in 0442's shape both shadow tables lose the row together and agree perfectly. **A1's independence from segment damage is exactly why it cannot see a fault that lives only in segments.** A2 -- the index's own docids via `fts5vocab` in `instance` mode, anti-joined against `%_content` -- **finds it: docid 2599, 122 distinct terms, 0.13 s on 169 MB**, the same two numbers the original investigation reached by a far more elaborate route. The four ruled parts: A2 is the detector; fts5's own `'integrity-check'` is the second witness and on 3.53.2 names the fault itself as `fts5: missing row %lld from content table %s`; **the shared failure mode is DECLARED in the output and in the issue** (both read segments, and `fts5vocab` was patched at 3.51.1), because a principle declared unsatisfied beats one satisfied with a decoy; and A1 survives as a THIRD arm for the shadow-tables-disagree question, cheap, labelled, **never counted as coverage.** **The highest-priority output requirement: A1 reading clean must not print as reassurance about the index**, or it rebuilds the exact defect 0442 exists to close, which is `doctor` and `index status` reading clean over real damage all night. Advisory, not blocking. `a2test.db` in the session scratchpad is the proof artefact; `dam.db` was never opened for writing.

**STILL DEAD, FROM DOING 15, BECAUSE EACH HAS A BANKED ARTEFACT ARGUING FOR IT.** (1) The phantom is NOT `a_sync_writes_no_render_the_store_has_moved_past.rs` -- added at 17:47:53Z, 1,626 s AFTER the damaged snapshot; **rowid 2599 was always right and the FILE attribution was the retracted part.** (2) No diff of the damaged copy against the REPAIRED copy is valid -- 55 minutes apart on a live estate; only a rebuild of the SAME database is a control, signature 0 add and 0 delete hunks. (3) The frequency enrichment is 1.33x, not 17x. (4) The stale-`iVersion` mechanism is refuted; the cookie moves anyway, measured with both controls. (5) Do not set secure-delete on before `replace_src_sections`' bulk DELETE: 13,435 ms against 485. **And 0442's CAUSE stays closed at eight negatives -- do not reopen it.** One loose end is now explained and owes a drive: the verb leaves version 4 while a replay leaves 5 because 3.46.0 gates the bump on `bUpdateOrDelete`, which only a DELETE, an UPDATE, or an INSERT under REPLACE-with-explicit-rowid sets -- never a plain INSERT. Drive it in the same run as the bump.

**THE RELEASE DRIVER, READ OFF `intent/docs/releasing.md` AT HEAD RATHER THAN ANY SUMMARY INCLUDING MINE AND vc's.** There IS a window between the tag and the push and **it cannot be used**: declining the confirmation exits 2 with the tag already local, and a re-run finds the tag at a different sha from the new HEAD and **refuses to force-move it**. So the regeneration and the notes are committed BEFORE the driver runs; v3.0.3 shipped the previous cut's reference pages because `a87a94a4a` landed 24 minutes after the tag and is not its ancestor. The baseline is `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` and **`--tags` is load-bearing** -- the bare form answers `v2.3.2` forever, because every v3 tag is lightweight. ic drove every command in that page and found four defects, so trust the page at HEAD and not a recollection of it.

**WHAT ELSE IS MINE AND WAITING.** The 3.1.0 notes are banked at `refs/bank/cc/release-notes/` (`CHANGELOG-3.1.0.md`, 112 bullets; `RELEASE_NOTES-3.1.0.md`, 25 KB bold-lead prose, no bullets -- the house form measured off 3.0.2). **Both assert that `intent doctor` does not detect 0442, in Provenance and in Upgrading, and the detector makes that false.** Revise when it lands. The seven known-defects lines stay SUPERSEDED and banked as input at `refs/bank/cc/release-notes/known-defects-lines.md`; the page is re-driven whole at the cut. `133d1363d` stays landed. Then the trawl carry: Part A is GO, Part B on vc's disposition, one mechanical commit per estate, doctor after each, vc checks each. 0443 moved to dc. NO RELEASE, NO PUSH.
